title: Identity-point composition normalization at all coefficient stages
statement:
Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $a:X	o s$ its structure morphism. Use the datum's constructible finite-Tor categories and exceptional adjunctions; at the integral stage use the completed operations with compatible etale-origin witnesses on finite reductions, at $E$ use their scalar localization, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use a common finite coefficient stage, on the corresponding domains of [fix-lem-exchanges]. Let $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}:R\mathrm{id}_{s!}Ra_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_!$ denote the specified compact-support composition comparison: the finite comparison of [thm-sf-comp-composition], its completed form, or its rationalized or common-stage form as in [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4), respectively. Under the canonical $R\mathrm{id}_{s!}\cong\mathrm{id}$ identification, $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}$ is the identity natural transformation at each of these stages.

Put $\omega_s=R\mathrm{id}_s^!\Lambda_s$ and let $
u:\omega_s	o\Lambda_s$ be the counit of $R\mathrm{id}_{s!}\dashv R\mathrm{id}_s^!$ under that same identity comparison. Let $c:Ra^!\omega_s	o Ra^!\Lambda_s$ be the inverse of the right-adjoint mate of $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}$; thus $c$ is the conjugate of $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}^{-1}$ with respect to $Ra_!\dashv Ra^!$ and the composite adjunction $R\mathrm{id}_{s!}Ra_!\dashv Ra^!R\mathrm{id}_s^!$ with pasted unit and counit. Then $
u$ and $c$ are isomorphisms, $c=Ra^!(
u)$, and, for the counit $\varepsilon^!_N:Ra_!Ra^!N	o N$ of $Ra_!\dashv Ra^!$,
$$\varepsilon^!_{\Lambda_s}\circ Ra_!(c)=
u\circ\varepsilon^!_{\omega_s}.$$
These are equations of morphisms in the actual category at the chosen coefficient stage. In particular the integral assertion is an assertion for the specified completed composition comparison itself.

source.place: Pairing-identification proof, normalization at the point; fix-lem-exchanges clauses (2),(4), completed and transported composition comparisons at (id_s,a)
